name: Event-market making: spread capture vs settlement carry, rebate wedge and taker-delay last look
seed_category: liquidity provision / market making - true spread capture
one_line: Two-sided quoting across many event markets where on-chain evidence says the rent is mostly settlement carry and selection, helped by the maker rebate, taker-fee wedge and matching delays.
scope: Cover the professional inventory business across politics/culture/tech/long-tail markets: who the ~800 bot accounts and institutional entrants (Wintermute etc.) are, PnL decomposition (91.4% of persistent makers' profit at settlement, median effective half-spread ~0, ~32 effective makers), role switching by skilled wallets, merge-based exits, toxicity/regime switching (poly-maker reference design), deterministic maker rebate per fill (0.19-0.35c/share at 50c), the taker-fee wedge, and venue matching delays (sports 1 s, crypto 50 ms) as a maker cancel option. Include the on-chain-vs-feed trade-direction caveat (59%). Boundary: subsidy-first quoting goes to maker-reward-pool-farming; 5m/15m crypto to short-crypto-maker-side; sportsbook-anchored sports quoting to sportsbook-anchored-sports-mm; longshot-side underwriting to longshot-selling-flb; theoretical quoting models (logit HJB, structural volatility) are in the speculative band.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Professional two-sided market making across event markets
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: High-frequency quoting across hundreds of markets for spread, rebates and rewards, run as an inventory business.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Post-only two-sided quotes around a microprice/flow-based fair value, inventory skew, volatility/toxicity widening and a regime switch that pulls quotes on news. Inventory exits by merging YES+NO pairs rather than crossing the spread. Income is spread + liquidity rewards + 15-25% of taker fees per market. The winners trade far more often, across more markets, and enter earlier at better prices than retail; one account made about $3M in 2026 on more than a million trades in Oscars markets alone.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Being the counterparty to late, price-insensitive retail flow; scale across the long tail (about 70% of closed markets had under $10k volume per a CNBC analysis, snippet only).
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: It is where the measured money is: bot-like accounts' gains mirror retail losses almost one for one. Institutions (Wintermute) are in, but specialists keep edges in niche, low-liquidity markets that large firms avoid.

evidence.title: Bots Are Winning Big on Polymarket (Newser summary of Bloomberg analysis)
evidence.supports: ~800 high-frequency bot accounts each cleared >$100k, ~$131M collectively Jan 2025-Apr 2026, mirroring $131M retail losses; bots trade more often, across more markets, enter earlier at better prices. Bloomberg original not fetchable.

evidence.supports: Reference architecture of the practice: maker-only BUY-YES/BUY-NO, merge exit, toxicity EWMA, QUIET/TRENDING/EVENT regimes; explicit warning that MM 'is competitive and can lose money'.

evidence.title: The Anatomy of a Decentralized Prediction Market (Dubach)
evidence.supports: 30B book events, 600 markets: longshot spread premium, near-uniform depth profile, maker-wallet diversity with concentrated tail; public-feed trade direction matches on-chain truth only ~59%, so markouts must use OrderFilled events.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: News jumps (binary payoff = gap risk to 0/1); adverse selection by insiders (documented 97% win-rate wallets); rebate/reward cuts by decree; record-level fills cannot identify quote lifecycle, so competitor analysis from chain data is limited.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Run poly-maker-style logic in paper mode on 20 long-dated political markets; attribute would-be PnL into spread, markout, rewards and rebates; go live only where markout loss < rewards+rebates.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Settlement-carry market making (screening rent)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Quote outside the informed-signal band, get filled mainly by uninformed tail demand, and earn by carrying the underpriced complementary claim to resolution rather than by capturing spread.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Post resting bids on the favoured side (0.50-1.00 band) wide enough that informed flow does not hit them first; uninformed longshot/tail buyers lift the other side, leaving the maker long the underpriced complement. Inventory is deliberately held to settlement instead of being flattened. In multi-outcome events the per-leg committed markup accumulates with the number of outcomes, so large negRisk fields pay more. Skilled wallets switch roles: they make in high-volume, short-duration markets and take elsewhere.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Adverse-selection screening plus the favourite-longshot premium paid by tail-demand takers; on-chain PnL shows the rent is realised at settlement.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Most retail MM bots optimise spread capture and inventory flattening, which this evidence says is ~0 on Polymarket; the rent belongs to whoever is willing to warehouse resolution risk with good selection.

evidence.title: Who Aggregates Information? Screening, Rent, and the Coexistence of CLOB and AMM Prediction Markets (Zang, Andrade, Nakajima), arXiv
evidence.supports: 588M Polymarket trades / $67B: 91.4% of persistent makers' profit arrives at settlement, <9% from pre-resolution spread capture; profit almost entirely from buying (+$70K vs +$2.6K selling, units as reported), concentrated at 0.50-0.80 (+$52.4K) and 0.80-1.00 (+$24.8K); set-completion cost rises +0.060 per outcome across 16,036 multi-outcome events, 96% of it committed markup; sample fee context: takers 1.8%, makers 0, no rebate.

evidence.title: Skilled Liquidity Provision in Prediction Markets: Evidence from 150 Million Trades (H.-C. Yang), SSRN via Crossref abstract
evidence.supports: Aggregate spread transfer is negligible; top-5% skilled traders earn $121 per market as makers and $63 as takers, extracting $228M over three years; ordinary traders lose on both sides; skilled wallets make more in higher-volume, shorter-duration markets; OOS persistence and wash-trade exclusions reported.

evidence.title: Who Wins and Who Loses in Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket (Akey, Gregoire, Harvie, Martineau), SSRN via Crossref abstract
evidence.supports: 2.4M users, $67B: top 1% capture 76.5% of gains; limit-order users benefit most; liquidity-taking drives losses - for ~1 in 5 losers the cost of taking liquidity alone flips PnL negative.

evidence.title: The Anatomy of a Decentralized Prediction Market (Dubach), arXiv
evidence.supports: Median effective half-spread on top-100 markets ~0 (-0.0003 prob pts); Glosten-Harris adverse-selection component median 0; quoted half-spread ~400 bps at mid prices, 1,300-1,800 bps below 0.10, 53 bps above 0.90; median maker HHI 0.031 (~32 effective makers).

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Regime dependence: in trending markets the longshot side is underpriced (+0.225 gap) and the favourite overpriced (-0.205), reversing the edge; warehouse risk is lumpy (resolution jump ~35% of total belief variance per Ando, SSRN 7086539); capital intensive; ghost-fill style counterparty attacks target exactly this inventory.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: From your own fill history split maker PnL into (a) round-trip spread PnL and (b) mark-to-settlement PnL by price band and by market regime (trending vs flippy); if (b) dominates, switch the inventory policy from flatten to carry in the bands where it is positive.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Rebate-aware maker quoting inside the taker-fee wedge
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: In fee-enabled categories the maker rebate is algebraically a fixed share of the fee generated by your own fills (0.19-0.35c per share at 50c) and the taker fee (1.0-1.75c at 50c) shields quotes from marginal informed flow; price both into the quoting model.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Takers pay fee = shares x feeRate x p x (1-p); makers pay nothing. Each market's rebate pool is 20% (crypto), 15% (sports) or 25% (all other fee categories) of that market's taker fees and is split by each maker's fee-equivalent on filled maker volume, which reduces to rebate% x the fee generated by your own fills. At p = 0.5 that is 0.35c/share in crypto, 0.19c in sports, 0.25c in politics/finance/tech/mentions and 0.31c in economics/culture/weather/other; it falls to zero toward the extremes. Rebates pay daily in pUSD above $1; post-only orders guarantee maker status. Because a taker must overcome up to 1.75c of fee, a maker can quote inside the band where true value has moved less than the fee without being profitably hit.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Structural fee asymmetry set by the venue: negative effective maker fee plus a protective taker cost, largest at mid-priced, high-turnover markets such as 5-minute and 15-minute crypto.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: On 0.1c-tick markets a 0.25-0.35c rebate is worth several ticks; quoters that ignore it are systematically too wide and lose queue priority to those that include it.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: High-tier takers pay only half the fee (Taker Rebate Program up to 50%), so the wedge is thinner against exactly the most informed flow; crypto taker delay was cut from 250ms to 50ms on 2026-08-17; rates change by changelog (sports rebate cut 25%->15% on 2026-07-10); some markets are zero-fee per feeSchedule and pay no rebate.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: From your own historical maker fills compute rebate% x fee per fill and compare with realised 1s/10s/60s markouts by category; this shows immediately in which categories rebate covers adverse selection.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Exploiting the asymmetric speed bump: maker last look under the taker delay
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: On delayed markets, takers are locked for 50-250 ms or more while makers can still cancel. Quote tighter than is otherwise safe and pull on the external signal.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Markets flagged for taker delay hold a marketable order and then re-validate it, and the taker cannot cancel in the meantime. A resting maker can cancel during that window. A maker subscribed to the driving signal (Binance or Chainlink for crypto, the score feed for sports) gets a free look before being hit. This works like FX last look or an IEX-style speed bump. The strategy quotes inside competitors who do not use the window, captures rebates (20% crypto, 15% sports), and re-widens when Polymarket shortens the delay. The delay went from 250 ms to 50 ms on crypto on 2026-08-17, and from 1 s to zero on the World Cup.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: A venue rule that shifts adverse-selection risk from makers to takers. The edge goes to the maker with the fastest cancel path.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: The rule is recent and its parameters change often, so whoever tracks the changelog and re-tunes first wins. It needs low-latency cancel infrastructure, not capital.
raw_discovery_candidates.adjacent_grounding: FX last look and the IEX and Aequitas speed bumps. No paper was found specific to Polymarket's delay, which is unverified.

evidence.title: Order Lifecycle, Polymarket docs
evidence.supports: Marketable orders on flagged markets are held for 250 ms and then re-validated. They cannot be cancelled while pending. Resting orders can be cancelled at any time before matching.

evidence.title: Polymarket changelog
evidence.supports: 'The taker delay on crypto markets is now 50ms, down from 250ms.' Also covers the Chainlink TWAP resolution changes of Aug 7 and 14.

evidence.title: Sandmark post on the 250 ms taker delay (search snippet only)
evidence.supports: Snippet: a 250 ms taker delay on crypto and finance markets from 5 June 2026, 'locking orders once they enter the delay window to reduce automated gaming by high-frequency bots'.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: At 50 ms the window is only useful to co-located bots. Polymarket can change or remove delays per market without notice. Everyone who is fast converges to the same tight quotes, and the rebate pool is split pro rata.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Measure your cancel round-trip against the delay per market, using the itode flag on /clob-markets. Simulate how many adverse fills you would have escaped at 50 ms and at 250 ms.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Matching delays as a maker's free option
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Quote tighter than fair-value uncertainty would normally allow in markets where marketable orders are held before matching (sports 1 s, crypto 50 ms, perps 20 ms), using a faster external feed to cancel inside the delay.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Polymarket holds marketable orders in a pending state on selected markets before re-validating and matching: Gamma shows secondsDelay = 1 on NFL game markets, the changelog sets the crypto taker delay at 50 ms (250 ms before 2026-08-17), and Perps applies 20 ms. The taker cannot cancel a pending marketable order, while resting makers can cancel freely. A maker with a sub-second sports data feed or a direct exchange price feed therefore sees the triggering event before the delayed taker order reaches its quote and can pull or reprice, which is economically a last-look right granted by the venue. The quoting engine keys spread width to (own feed latency minus venue delay) rather than to event volatility alone; order responses return status 'delayed', and market.trading.secondsDelay is readable per market.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Venue-designed asymmetry between takers and makers; monetised by whoever has the fastest relevant external data.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: In sports with a 1 s hold, a maker on a 300-500 ms scores feed avoids most goal/score pick-offs and can earn the concentrated live rewards at tighter spreads than competitors.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Delay shrinks over time (crypto already cut 5x); liquidity programmes can impose minimum rest times (3.5 s in March Madness) that neutralise fast cancels; cancel rate limits; competitors with official low-latency data.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: For one weekend, timestamp your feed's score events against the first book move on Polymarket; if your feed leads by more than the cancel round-trip but less than 1 s, the option has value.
